feedback.finish: Everyone can decide what they do or don’t want to share.

atoms.finishSound: Privacy means being able to keep something to yourself and having your own space.

instruction.text: Decide whether each activity is something done in private or in public.

trainers.hint: If you’re finding it hard to decide, think about whether you would want a stranger to see you doing it.

instruction.text: Select the pieces of clothing that help us cover up our private parts.

feedback.end: Some parts of our body should only be seen by ourselves and the people we trust the most. That’s why we wear swimming costumes or trunks at the pool and keep our underwear on while getting changed for PE at school.

trainers.instruction: Decide if the statement is true or false.

atoms.a: Only adults have a right to privacy.
Privacy can mean keeping certain information from other people.
Privacy can mean only sharing some parts of yourself or your life with trusted people.
We wear underwear to cover our private parts.
